learningObjective: Each successful radius around each odd or even center identifies exactly one distinct palindromic substring occurrence.

mechanismReview.pattern: Count successful expansions from every odd and even center.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: The task counts contiguous palindrome occurrences, including equal text at different positions, so each center-radius pair should contribute separately.
mechanismReview.invariant: Each successful while iteration adds one new palindrome for that center and then expands one cell outward. Completed centers contribute disjoint occurrences because every palindrome has one unique center.
mechanismReview.stateModel: Keep middle, left, right, a local expansion count, and the outer sum. Characters remain unchanged and no set is needed because occurrences, not distinct values, are counted.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: An indexed character row with stable middle/L/R keys exposes odd and even center geometry and lists every accepted range, contribution, mismatch or boundary stop, and running sum.
rejectedAlternatives: A set of palindrome strings incorrectly merges duplicate occurrences.
A final count of six does not show the three singles, two pairs, and one triple.
A DP matrix is valid but heavier than the constant-space implementation.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: Map each combinatorial object to a unique center and radius, then count every successful expansion once; the same enumeration underlies longest-palindrome and palindrome-radius algorithms.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.

deckReview.notes: No source slide deck is part of the supplied coding guide. The visual was designed from this problem's source implementation and worked trace.

sourceReview.notes: The supplied Coding_Questions_Phone_Guide.md is the curriculum source. The task, implementation sketch, and complexity statement are preserved; the trace frames are original explanatory artwork.
